article.title: A Good Dashboard Should Tell You What Changed Before Telling You Why
article.author: OpenAI learning editor
article.why: 把資料分析中最容易混淆的描述與解釋拆開，特別適合 CVR、構成比與 population mix 類問題。

paragraphs.en: Dashboards are designed to help people understand a business quickly, but they often create a subtle problem: they mix description and explanation. A chart shows that conversion fell, and the next sentence immediately says that customer interest weakened. The first statement may be supported by data. The second is a hypothesis. When the two are presented together, decision makers can forget that one is observed and the other still needs to be tested.
paragraphs.zh: Dashboard 的目的，是幫助人快速理解業務，但它常產生一個隱性問題：把描述和解釋混在一起。圖表顯示 conversion 下降，下一句就直接說顧客興趣變弱。前者可能有資料支持，後者則仍是需要驗證的假設。
paragraphs.ja: ダッシュボードは業務を素早く理解するためのものですが、「何が起きたか」と「なぜ起きたか」を混ぜる危険があります。コンバージョンが下がったという事実と、顧客関心が低下したという仮説は別です。

paragraphs.en: A stronger dashboard starts with a disciplined question: what exactly changed? If conversion moved from 12 percent to 10 percent, analysts should first inspect the numerator and denominator. Did the number of purchases fall, did traffic rise, or did both change? A ratio can move even when the behavior in the numerator is stable. For example, a campaign that attracts many low-intent visitors can reduce conversion even if the number of buyers remains unchanged.
paragraphs.zh: 更好的 dashboard 應先問：到底改變了什麼？如果 conversion 從 12% 降到 10%，先拆 numerator 與 denominator。是購買數下降、流量上升，還是兩者都變？大量低意圖流量進來時，即使買家數沒變，conversion 也會下降。
paragraphs.ja: 例えばコンバージョンが12％から10％へ下がった場合、まず分子と分母を確認します。購入数が減ったのか、流入が増えたのか、両方なのかを分けます。低意向ユーザーが大量に流入すれば、購入者数が同じでも率は下がります。

paragraphs.en: Population mix creates another common trap. Suppose Android users convert at 17 percent and iOS users at 9 percent. If the share of iOS traffic suddenly grows, total conversion can fall even when conversion improves within both device groups. The aggregate result looks worse, but the underlying segment performance is better. This is not a statistical curiosity; it changes the management response. A product problem requires different action from a traffic-mix problem.
paragraphs.zh: Population mix 是另一個常見陷阱。假設 Android conversion 17%、iOS 9%，如果 iOS 流量占比突然升高，即使兩個裝置內部 conversion 都改善，整體 conversion 仍可能下降。表面看起來變差，但 segment 內部表現其實變好。產品問題和流量組成問題需要完全不同的對策。
paragraphs.ja: 構成比も重要です。Androidが17％、iOSが9％のとき、iOS比率が高まれば、両セグメントの率が改善していても全体率は低下する場合があります。全体悪化とセグメント悪化は同じ意味ではありません。

paragraphs.en: For that reason, a useful dashboard should separate three layers. The first layer reports the outcome: what metric changed, by how much, and over what period. The second layer decomposes the outcome into components such as volume, rate, segment, channel, geography, or customer cohort. The third layer presents possible causes with evidence strength clearly labeled. This structure prevents a plausible story from becoming an accepted fact too early.
paragraphs.zh: 因此 dashboard 最好分成三層。第一層只報結果：哪個指標改了、改多少、在哪個期間。第二層做 decomposition，例如 volume、rate、segment、channel、地域或 cohort。第三層才提出可能原因，並清楚標示證據強弱。
paragraphs.ja: 良いダッシュボードは三層に分けられます。第一は結果、第二は数量・率・セグメント・チャネルなどへの分解、第三は原因仮説です。原因には証拠の強さを示し、もっともらしい説明を早く事実扱いしないことが重要です。

paragraphs.en: Analysts should also check whether the measurement system changed. Tracking code may have been updated, event definitions may have moved, filters may have changed, or missing data may have increased. A dashboard can be numerically correct and still describe a different population from last month. Versioned metric definitions and data-quality checks therefore belong beside business charts, not in a separate technical appendix.
paragraphs.zh: 分析師也必須檢查 measurement system 是否改變。例如 tracking code、event definition、filter 或 missing data 都可能讓同一個指標其實描述不同 population。Dashboard 數字可以計算正確，卻不再與上月可比。
paragraphs.ja: 計測方法の変更も確認します。イベント定義、フィルター、トラッキング、欠損率が変われば、数字は正しくても比較対象が変わっている可能性があります。指標定義のバージョン管理は分析品質の一部です。

paragraphs.en: There is a trade-off. Executives do not want a dashboard filled with every diagnostic table. Too much detail destroys the purpose of a dashboard. The answer is not to show everything but to build a clear drill-down path. The headline should be simple, while the supporting analysis should be one click or one section away. The key is that the headline never claims more certainty than the evidence supports.
paragraphs.zh: 管理層不想看一堆診斷表。解法不是全部塞進首頁，而是提供清楚 drill-down 路徑。Headline 可以簡潔，但 supporting analysis 要能快速進入，而且 headline 不能比證據更有把握。
paragraphs.ja: 経営層へすべての診断表を見せる必要はありません。見出しは簡潔にし、必要な分解へすぐ移れる構造を作ります。重要なのは、見出しが証拠以上の確信を示さないことです。

paragraphs.en: A practical review routine can help. Before discussing causes, the team asks four questions: Is the movement real? Which component changed? Which segments explain most of the movement? Did any definition or data source change? Only after those questions are answered should the discussion move to why the change happened and what action to take. This order protects the team from spending time on a story that fits the chart but not the data-generating process.
paragraphs.zh: 實務上，可以在討論原因前固定問四個問題：這個變化是真的嗎？哪個 component 變了？哪些 segment 解釋了大部分變動？定義或資料來源有沒有改？回答完，再討論原因與行動。
paragraphs.ja: 原因議論の前に、「変化は本物か」「どの要素が変わったか」「どのセグメントが寄与したか」「定義やデータ源は変わったか」を確認すると、誤った問題へ対策するリスクを減らせます。

paragraphs.en: The broader lesson is that dashboards should protect decision quality, not merely display numbers. A good dashboard makes uncertainty visible. It distinguishes observation from interpretation, aggregate movement from segment movement, and business change from measurement change. That discipline may add a few minutes to analysis, but it can prevent weeks of work aimed at solving the wrong problem.
paragraphs.zh: 好的 dashboard 不只是展示數字，而是保護決策品質。它把 observation 與 interpretation、aggregate 與 segment、business change 與 measurement change 清楚分開。多花幾分鐘，往往能避免幾週都在解錯問題。
paragraphs.ja: 良いダッシュボードは数字を表示するだけでなく、意思決定品質を守るものです。観測と解釈、全体変化とセグメント変化、業務変化と計測変化を分けることが重要です。

vocabulary.usage: a larger denominator can lower the rate
treat the explanation as a hypothesis
a plausible story is not proof
population mix can move the total rate
check whether the measurement system changed

phrases.example: Before discussing causes, ask what exactly changed.
Let’s break down the movement by device and channel.
Do we have evidence to support the claim?

phrases.explanation: 說出看似合理但未驗證的故事。
phrases.example: The chart tells a plausible story, but we still need evidence.
The campaign changed the denominator more than the numerator.
We should drill into the iOS segment before deciding.

grammar.title: A ratio can move even when the behavior in the numerator is stable.
grammar.body: even when 表示即使條件成立，結果仍可能不同。

grammar.title: Only after those questions are answered should the discussion move to why.
grammar.body: Only after 置首時使用倒裝，適合正式商務寫作。

grammar.title: The answer is not to show everything but to build a clear drill-down path.
grammar.body: not A but B 用來糾正錯誤二分法。

grammar.title: A dashboard can be numerically correct and still describe a different population.
grammar.body: can be A and still B 表示兩件看似矛盾的事可同時成立。

business.example: Let’s separate observation from interpretation before we discuss actions.

business.term: Can we decompose the movement by segment?
business.example: Can we decompose the movement by device and channel?
Before calling this a performance issue, has the denominator changed?
What evidence supports that explanation beyond the headline chart?
Did the metric definition change between the two periods?

quiz.question: Why can total conversion fall even if each device segment improves?
quiz.answer: Because the traffic mix can shift toward a lower-converting segment.

quiz.question: What four questions should be asked before discussing causes?
quiz.answer: Is the movement real, which component changed, which segments explain it, and did the definition or source change?

quiz.question: Output: explain a KPI change using numerator, denominator, and population mix in 100 words.
quiz.answer: Use one business example and clearly separate observation from hypothesis.

interpretation.label: 核心
interpretation.text: 先描述 what changed，再提出 why。

interpretation.label: 資料分析
interpretation.text: 比例指標一定要拆 numerator、denominator 與 population mix。

interpretation.label: 風險
interpretation.text: measurement change 可能被誤認成 business change。
